Sylvester Tegetmeier
sil-ves'ter tay'get-my-er
n. (d. 1552; preacher at St James's in Riga, the fiercer of the city's two reformers)
Tegetmeier, a Low German occupational surname, a Meier or steward of a Teget holding; Sylvester, from Latin silvestris, of the woods.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Sylvester Tegetmeier was a Rostock man who studied there and at Wittenberg and came to Riga in 1522 to preach at St James's. Where Knopken taught, Tegetmeier denounced. He preached against the images, the mass and the monasteries in terms the crowds understood immediately, and in March 1524 a mob went through the Riga churches and destroyed the images and altars; Tegetmeier had preached the sermons that lit it, and the councils of the city spent years repairing the damage to its order and its own legitimacy. He later quarrelled with Knopken and with the council, and served at St James's until his death in 1552. The dictionary records him because the second commandment is true and the riot was still wrong, and the two have to be said together: “Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image” (Exo 20:4), and “Let all things be done decently and in order” (1Co 14:40).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines an image as a representation of a person or thing, an idol; iconoclast as a breaker or destroyer of images; and decently as in a becoming manner, with propriety of behaviour.

expand to see more

IMAGE, n. [L. imago.] A representation or similitude of any person or thing, formed of a material substance; an idol; the object of idolatrous worship.

ICONOCLAST, n. [Gr. eikon, an image, and klao, to break.] A breaker or destroyer of images; one who opposes the worship of images.

DECENTLY, adv. In a decent or becoming manner; with propriety of behaviour; without immodesty.

ZEAL, n. [Gr. zelos.] Passionate ardor in the pursuit of any thing; enthusiasm; it may be good or bad according to its object.

ORDER, n. Regular disposition; methodical arrangement; established mode of proceeding; rule.

Key Scripture

Exo 20:4 — "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:"

Isa 42:8 — "I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images."

Psa 115:4 — "Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands."

1Co 14:40 — "Let all things be done decently and in order."

Modern Corruption

Preacher at St James's in Riga from 1522 whose sermons touched off the iconoclasm of March 1524; quarrelled with Knopken and with the council; died 1552.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The entry does have to hold two things that are usually separated. Tegetmeier was right about the images: the second commandment forbids them in worship, and the Riga churches were full of objects men had been taught to venerate. He was wrong about the mob. A congregation turned loose on its own building has not obeyed the commandment; it has substituted its own zeal for the magistrate's duty and the church's order, and it taught Riga's council for a generation to associate the gospel with wreckage.

The principle to recover is that both halves are commanded. God's refusal to share his glory with an artefact is absolute and his own: “I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images” (Isa 42:8), and the idols are weighed for what they are — “Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands” (Psa 115:4). But the reform of worship is itself to be a reform, not a riot: “Let all things be done decently and in order” (1Co 14:40). Zeal that will not wait for order is not obedience in a hurry; it is a different sin.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew pesel (H6459), a graven image; Greek euschemonos (G2156), decently.

Hebrew pesel (H6459) — a carved or graven image, an idol; Exodus 20:4.

Hebrew temunah (H8544) — a likeness, a form, a similitude; Exodus 20:4.

Hebrew kabod (H3519) — glory, weight, honour; “my glory will I not give to another”, Isaiah 42:8.

Hebrew 'atsab (H6091) — an idol, a thing shaped; Psalm 115:4.

Greek euschemonos (G2156) — becomingly, decently, honourably; 1 Corinthians 14:40.

Usage

"“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image” (Exo 20:4) — preaching against the images at St James's from 1522."

"“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands” (Psa 115:4) — the Riga iconoclasm of March 1524."

"“Let all things be done decently and in order” (1Co 14:40) — the standard by which the riot is judged and found wanting."
